newsitem.title: USA: Bull HN says shuts part of plant in Brighton, Mass.
newsitem.headline: Bull HN says shuts part of plant in Brighton, Mass.

text.p: Bull HN Information Systems Tuesday confirmed that it shut part of its plant in Brighton, Mass., adding it has cut its fulltime workforce to about 250, about half what it totaled in June.

Steve Puleo, a company spokesman, said the cutbacks, first reported in the Boston Globe Tuesday, reflected a decision to switch from making circuit boards for its own operations to assemblying them for other suppliers.
The U.S. operation is owned by Compagnie Machine Bull of France.
Puleo explained that assemblying circuit boards for other companies, from telecommunications firms to ones that make precision instruments, was more profitable.

Around 60 jobs were lost when the plant's board fabrication unit was closed in August, while another 190 positions were shed in the summer as sales fell and the company trimmed expenses, according to Boston Globe.
Puleo, who declined to comment on the company's plans for the Brighton plant, added he might have more information shortly.
